```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(NetCoMi)
```

Differential networks are a further possibility to compare two microbial
association networks. In a differential network, two nodes are connected if
their association differs between the two groups.

`diffnet()` provides four methods for identifying differentially associated
taxa pairs:

* `"threshold"`: simple thresholding of absolute association differences.
* `"fisherTest"`: Fisher's z-test for comparing correlations between two groups.
* `"permute"`: a permutation test with re-estimation of associations after
  permuting group labels.
* `"discordant"`: the discordant method for detecting differential
  correlations.

We start by dividing the amgut data set into two groups: samples with and
without seasonal allergies.

```{r}
data("amgut2.filt.phy")

# Split the phyloseq object into two groups
amgut_season_yes <- phyloseq::subset_samples(amgut2.filt.phy,
                                             SEASONAL_ALLERGIES == "yes")
amgut_season_no <- phyloseq::subset_samples(amgut2.filt.phy,
                                            SEASONAL_ALLERGIES == "no")

amgut_season_yes
amgut_season_no
```

Due to its short execution time, we use Pearson's correlations for estimating
associations between OTUs. `sparsMethod` is set to `"none"` so that all
estimated associations remain available for the association-network plots below.
The differential network itself is always based on the estimated association
matrices before sparsification, namely the `assoEst1` and `assoEst2` matrices
returned by `netConstruct()`.

```{r netconstruct}
net_season_pears <- netConstruct(data = amgut_season_no,
                                 data2 = amgut_season_yes,
                                 filtTax = "highestVar",
                                 filtTaxPar = list(highestVar = 50),
                                 measure = "pearson",
                                 normMethod = "clr",
                                 sparsMethod = "none",
                                 thresh = 0.2,
                                 verbose = 3)

props_season_pears <- netAnalyze(net_season_pears,
                                 clustMethod = "cluster_fast_greedy",
                                 weightDeg = TRUE,
                                 normDeg = FALSE)
```

## Thresholding absolute association differences

The threshold method is the simplest and most flexible way to construct a
differential network. It keeps all taxa pairs whose absolute difference in
estimated association exceeds `diffThresh`. It does not perform a statistical
test or multiple testing adjustment, and is therefore useful as an exploratory
screening method or whenever a practical effect-size threshold is desired.

```{r diffnet_threshold, fig.height=20, fig.width=25}
diff_season_thresh <- diffnet(net_season_pears,
                              diffMethod = "threshold",
                              diffThresh = 0.3)

plot(diff_season_thresh,
     cexNodes = 0.8,
     cexLegend = 3,
     cexTitle = 4,
     mar = c(2,2,8,10),
     legendGroupnames = c("group 'no'", "group 'yes'"),
     legendPos = c(0.9,1.6),
     legendArgs = list(lwd = 8))
```

Edge colors represent the signs of the associations in the two groups. For
example, an edge colored according to `+ | -` indicates that the two taxa are
positively associated in group 1 and negatively associated in group 2.

We can also inspect the corresponding association networks. First, we compute a
layout for all taxa in the two association networks. Since the layout matrix has
taxon names as row names, it can be reused for the differential network and is
matched to the plotted nodes by name.

```{r association_layout}
p_all <- plot(props_season_pears,
              sameLayout = TRUE,
              layoutGroup = "union",
              rmSingles = FALSE,
              doPlot = FALSE)
```

Next, we plot the association networks for the taxa that occur in the threshold
differential network. The layout is a subset of the full layout created above.

```{r asso_networks_threshold, fig.height=19, fig.width=40}
diffmat_sums_thresh <- rowSums(diff_season_thresh$diffMat)
diff_asso_names_thresh <- names(diffmat_sums_thresh[diffmat_sums_thresh > 0])

p <- plot(props_season_pears,
          nodeFilter = "names",
          nodeFilterPar = diff_asso_names_thresh,
          layout = p_all$layout$layout1[diff_asso_names_thresh, , drop = FALSE],
          nodeColor = "gray",
          highlightHubs = FALSE,
          sameLayout = TRUE,
          layoutGroup = "union",
          rmSingles = FALSE,
          nodeSize = "clr",
          edgeTranspHigh = 20,
          labelScale = FALSE,
          cexNodes = 1.5,
          cexLabels = 3,
          cexTitle = 3.8,
          groupNames = c("No seasonal allergies", "Seasonal allergies"),
          hubBorderCol  = "gray40")

legend(-0.15,-0.7, title = "estimated correlation:", legend = c("+","-"),
       col = c("#009900","red"), inset = 0.05, cex = 4, lty = 1, lwd = 4,
       bty = "n", horiz = TRUE)
```

The same layout can now be used for the differential network. By keeping the
default `rmSingles = TRUE`, taxa without differential associations are removed
from the differential network, and the named layout matrix is subset to the
same taxa shown in the association-network plot above.

```{r diffnet_threshold_same_layout, fig.height=20, fig.width=25}
plot(diff_season_thresh,
     layout = p_all$layout$layout1,
     cexNodes = 0.8,
     cexLegend = 3,
     cexTitle = 4,
     mar = c(2,2,8,10),
     legendGroupnames = c("group 'no'", "group 'yes'"),
     legendPos = c(0.9,1.6),
     legendArgs = list(lwd = 8))
```

## Fisher's z-test

Fisher's z-test compares correlations between the two groups. Here, multiple
testing adjustment is done by controlling the local false discovery rate.

```{r diffnet_fisher, fig.height=20, fig.width=25}
diff_season_fisher <- diffnet(net_season_pears,
                              diffMethod = "fisherTest",
                              adjust = "lfdr")

plot(diff_season_fisher,
     cexNodes = 0.8,
     cexLegend = 3,
     cexTitle = 4,
     mar = c(2,2,8,10),
     legendGroupnames = c("group 'no'", "group 'yes'"),
     legendPos = c(0.9,1.6),
     legendArgs = list(lwd = 8))
```

## Permutation test

The permutation test randomly reassigns samples to the two groups while keeping
the group sizes fixed. Associations are re-estimated for each permuted data set,
which makes this method more computationally demanding than Fisher's z-test.
The chunks in this section are not evaluated in the vignette to keep build time
short.

```{r diffnet_permute, eval=FALSE, fig.height=20, fig.width=25}
diff_season_perm <- diffnet(net_season_pears,
                            diffMethod = "permute",
                            nPerm = 1000L,
                            cores = 4L,
                            adjust = "lfdr",
                            seed = 123456)

plot(diff_season_perm,
     cexNodes = 0.8,
     cexLegend = 3,
     cexTitle = 4,
     mar = c(2,2,8,10),
     legendGroupnames = c("group 'no'", "group 'yes'"),
     legendPos = c(0.9,1.6),
     legendArgs = list(lwd = 8))
     legendArgs = list(lwd = 8))
```

Permutation association matrices can also be stored and reused, which is helpful
when trying different multiple testing adjustments without repeating the full
permutation procedure.

```{r diffnet_permute_store, eval=FALSE}
diff_season_perm <- diffnet(net_season_pears,
                            diffMethod = "permute",
                            nPerm = 1000L,
                            cores = 4L,
                            adjust = "lfdr",
                            storeAssoPerm = TRUE,
                            fileStoreAssoPerm = "assoPerm",
                            seed = 123456)

diff_season_perm_bh <- diffnet(net_season_pears,
                               diffMethod = "permute",
                               nPerm = 1000L,
                               adjust = "BH",
                               fileLoadAssoPerm = "assoPerm")
```

## Discordant method

The discordant method is available through the optional `discordant`
Bioconductor package. It is shown here as non-evaluated code because the package
may not be installed.

```{r diffnet_discordant, eval=FALSE, fig.height=20, fig.width=25}
diff_season_discordant <- diffnet(net_season_pears,
                                  diffMethod = "discordant",
                                  discordThresh = 0.8,
                                  seed = 123456)

plot(diff_season_discordant,
     cexNodes = 0.8,
     cexLegend = 3,
     cexTitle = 4,
     mar = c(2,2,8,10),
     legendGroupnames = c("group 'no'", "group 'yes'"),
     legendPos = c(0.9,1.6),
     legendArgs = list(lwd = 8))
```
